interpretations.heading: Measurement layers and controlled comparisons
interpretations.text: Separate asset acquisition (bytes, download and cache), initialization (worker, model, runtime compilation and device resolution), audio preparation (fetch, decode, resampling and features), inference (first useful text and decode), post-processing (token decoding, normalization and selection), and product lifecycle (ready, stop-to-final, save and detail hydration). RTF is decode milliseconds divided by audio duration in milliseconds. Cold means empty cache and first initialization; warm means cached assets with a new pipeline; hot means the same worker/pipeline reused. Record actual cache evidence: an assumption about a browser cache does not establish worker cache state. Do not compare cold candidate results with warm baseline results or label total adapter initialization as pure model load.

interpretations.heading: Attributing a performance or accuracy gap
interpretations.text: Validate the instrument with a known baseline before interpreting a candidate. Use the same content-safe audio and observed model/runtime/device identity; record actual microphone settings, input-buffer/sample identity and requested versus observed configuration. A null-engine control isolates harness overhead; direct-pipeline, worker and app comparisons distinguish runtime, marshalling and product-lifecycle delays. Start with the product/app journey when runnable; stop decomposition on a clear accepted result. Use worker, direct-pipeline and component breakdowns only to answer an unavailable, ambiguous or failing higher-layer question, then return to the product journey for acceptance. A failed direct viability check must not be promoted into app integration. Comparisons need varied short, conversational, long, natural and noisy inputs rather than one eight-word fixture; record browser/GPU identity, dtype, requested/resolved device, fallback and cold penalty alongside timing. A direct decode, a worker result or a baseline-versus-baseline smoke cannot substitute for app qualification. Do not prescribe a DSP, resampler, VAD, model-size or timeout fix from a hypothesis or a faster short fixture alone.

interpretations.heading: Capture and lifecycle counterexamples
interpretations.text: Preserve immediate-speech and leading-filler input, sustained onset, leading silence, soft speech, trailing words, low-energy tails, long-form speech and a no-speech control. Trace inference completion through callback, store application and visible rendering before attributing first-text delay. A setup flag is not evidence the intended model or VAD executed: missing runtime identity, HTML returned as a model/WASM asset, unsupported model type or fallback must be named and must not enter a quality comparison. Setup consent, truthful model size/progress and prompt, actionable initialization failure remain separate from accuracy. Do not repair an onset/tail failure by silently dropping genuine speech.

interpretations.heading: Watchdog and final-text integrity controls
interpretations.text: Startup grace and ongoing liveness are separate controls: a fresh engine without its first pulse must not produce a false frozen warning, while a worker that never pulses or is deliberately killed must still fail within the governed bound. Check both controller and service warnings. Preserve original negative controls for repeated provisional text, repeated saved candidates, missing opening words and hallucinated tail text. A display-only deduplication is not a saved-transcript fix. Never collapse or rewrite ambiguous repetitions in the authoritative saved transcript to improve a score; classify the risk and preserve data integrity. Finalization, next Start, cancellation/navigation and microphone-track teardown require their own observed outcomes.

interpretations.heading: Inherited thresholds and promotion boundaries
interpretations.text: Older proposals for a 30% speed advantage, a 93.89% accuracy ceiling, a 15–20-point improvement, a 10% VAD timing tolerance, or a 90-second beta finalization allowance are historical experiment or release decisions, not newly approved limits for the selected deployment. Keep the original values with their dated evidence. Current model selection requires its own predeclared policy, representative corpus/device population and explicit owner decision; do not tune the policy from observed outcomes. Tiny/base/small, v4 dtype/backend and Moonshine experiments do not create customer choices, revive retired URL/PostHog selectors, or select work for the current Private v2 release.

interpretations.heading: Open Mic and returning-user acceptance controls
interpretations.text: Retain separate assertions for real signup/admission and authoritative account/plan binding; Products navigation with no microphone activation; truthful acquisition versus initialization timing and observed runtime; navigating away before Start completes without a later microphone start; live and saved filler agreement; exactly-once automatic save at Stop; two distinct speech-relevant coaching suggestions and one next action; review without reload; exact-session History/detail, reload and PDF equality; revisit without coaching regeneration; feedback acknowledgement, stored row and independently received telemetry; next Start without false finalizing debt; ended microphone tracks and exactly one Progress evaluation. The inherited next-Start ≤15-second control must remain identifiable until the receiver explicitly reconciles its bound, not silently disappear. Returning-user proof uses existing credentials and preserves plan, history and account state; navigation must write nothing and must not delete a maintained account. Prior mocked/CI successes do not close these deployed or human assertions.

interpretations.heading: Focus Points acceptance controls
interpretations.text: Preserve separate full and partial Focus journeys: topic and four points visible beside the transcript while pending, no microphone before Start, correct product/runtime identity, ordered speech-bound marker judgments, timing relative to the actual spoken point, no premature negative verdict before Stop, honest paraphrase handling and an unspoken point remaining missing. Preserve the inherited ≤5-second marker control separately from human timing perception until its bound is explicitly reconciled. Final coverage, per-point verdicts, average time per point, not-detected explanation and coaching must agree with the saved record and exact-session Analytics after reload. A partial fixture's 3/4 is not the full fixture's 4/4. The next-point selector chooses the first uncovered point; an unchanged index while that point remains pending is not by itself a failure or a PASS. A repeat take and a fresh Open Mic take must not inherit the wrong session or Focus state.

interpretations.heading: Feedback storage and request-binding controls
interpretations.text: Keep separate controls for successful coaching followed by feedback; unavailable/provider error; transport failure or timeout; delayed answer with total/provider latency; storage transport failure; explicit server rejection; stored row with lost reply; feedback about an older take; feedback with no session; and feedback from a repeat take. Acknowledgement follows confirmed storage. A failed/rejected write keeps the draft and reports the failure; retries must create one stored row, including when the first reply was lost. Older-take feedback must not acquire the current attempt; no-session feedback has no invented association; repeat feedback binds the repeat. Missing evidence is HOLD and contradictory evidence is FAIL, never an inferred successful diagnostic chain.

interpretations.heading: Independent coaching diagnostic binding
interpretations.text: Bind diagnostic_request_id and diagnostic_attempt_id at the outgoing invocation boundary to the verified saved session, and independently match the received diagnostic record. The stored report reference is metadata.coaching_diagnostic_ref; the feedback event carries coaching_diagnostic_id. UI tap order or the report alone does not bind a request. Keep endpoint HTTP class, provider HTTP class, product failureCategory and closed serverReason distinct; unknown source is acceptable only for a validated pre-provider failure. Independently recompute the server prompt digest from the actual outgoing inputs before calling prompt binding qualified; a recorded digest alone is not proof. Missing original request receipts or an authorized failure-injection mechanism remain explicit evidence gaps. Scoped support lookup, fault injection and account cleanup require their own authority; this control grants none.

interpretations.heading: Human evidence and coaching-copy boundaries
interpretations.text: Real microphone permission/copy, visible mobile Stop confirmation, acoustically realized uh, relevance of Open Mic coaching and whether Focus coaching addresses the spoken points require human observations. Synthetic speech, pre-granted permission, viewport emulation and a rendered coaching pair do not replace them. Keep the about 8–10-word coaching target soft; the retired six-word cap must not return and longer valid phrases are not rejected solely for length. Preserve the source distinction between the old What to improve heading and later Try this next run / What to try next wording; current product-copy acceptance, not a label alias in a test, decides equivalence. Receipt rows, requirements, journeys and human observations keep separate denominators.

interpretations.heading: Boundary debugging and test execution reference
interpretations.text: Prefer real implementations, then governed E2E configuration, then the test registry, with local mocks last; use real stores with explicit reset where practical. Reproduce the responsible boundary and confirm the original counterexample with meaningful positive and negative controls. Use actual service payloads, observable readiness and document/attempt identity; a selector or sent event proves only its own boundary. Report trace source, observation window, loss and settlement. Registered development commands include pnpm quality, pnpm test:unit, pnpm test:full, pnpm test:infra, pnpm test:e2e and pnpm ci:local; inspect current package scripts and host interlocks before execution. A focused pass is not full quality/CI, and rc:gates includes live work. Mocked paths do not prove hosted RLS, providers, hardware or customer acceptance. Preserve exact source/config, commands, named assertions, failures, unavailable observations and limits; do not dump private speech, coaching or credentials.

interpretations.heading: Known-speech filler diagnostics
interpretations.text: Optional known-speech diagnostics compare canonical live/persisted counts, diagnostic transcript recount and an acoustically verified reference; a discrepancy does not authorize changing the count source. Retain three original controls: the static script has um×3, so×2, like×2, uh×1 and basically×1 (nine all-key occurrences); the honestly custom-word script has three occurrences; the no-filler script has zero. Nine all-key occurrences is not nine coachable um/uh/ah fillers. Raw custom words must be represented by custom_N identifiers in artifacts. Preserve completeness: missing or malformed observations are not measured zero. Historical clarity/score diagnostic fields do not revive the retired universal score. The original verbatim public fixture text is preserved in the clause receipt; use only the selected Private customer path and separately authorized operator execution, not the historical Cloud/Native mode matrix.

interpretations.heading: Journey execution and cleanup boundaries
interpretations.text: Before an authorized run, bind the selected served frontend, backend and schema evidence to the frozen execution manifest. Repository main may advance through tooling-only merges; do not require main to equal the served product without inspecting component scope. Keep run-owned accounts separate from maintained accounts. Record received, sent-only, unobservable and missing telemetry separately, including settled action binding for feedback. Cleanup needs a post-delete residue check; policy-retained feedback must have its user link cleared. Stop on identity drift, unplanned provider failure, interruption or uncertain cleanup. Historical runbook instructions to start now, repair credentials or retry do not authorize a new window, account mutation or fault injection.

interpretations.heading: Completion and retention failure boundaries
interpretations.text: Preserve the distinction between a durable session/metrics write and successful transcript retention. A retention failure must not be presented as a lost session or a retained transcript; report the structured outcome and sanitized reason. Retention convergence, fresh completion, idempotent replay and conflicting replay need separate controls. Do not claim that in-memory retry content survives reload or that a content-free recovery draft can reconstruct a transcript. Progress must follow the authoritative successful metrics/session result rather than an obsolete secondary PATCH. Server-enforced character and UTF-8 byte bounds reject oversize input rather than silently truncating it. The historical #1314 values and two-transcript rotation are dated design evidence; the current newest-one contract governs acceptance.

interpretations.heading: Database proof and rollback interpretation
interpretations.text: A catalog readback that prints state and exits zero is diagnostic, not an enforcing gate. Prove grants, signatures, schema-cache resolution and the applicable retention coordinator with the actual target migrations; a single-connection simulation cannot establish concurrent lock contention. A full named-argument PostgREST probe distinguishes resolution from an invalid empty-call signature; PGRST202 alone does not establish which migration is absent. Preserve failure-injection evidence for partial application and PUBLIC EXECUTE exposure; do not assume CLI transaction wrapping. Rollback must restore all intended objects atomically, and a client already using a new RPC must be reverted before that RPC is removed. These are acceptance boundaries, not authority to apply the old packet or execute rollback.

interpretations.heading: Historical inventory does not authorize secret deletion
interpretations.text: Separate repository, environment, organization, frontend-build and Edge/DB runtime scopes. Zero workflow references do not establish that a runtime secret is unused, and an inaccessible organization inventory is unknown rather than empty. Duplicate Secret-to-Variable retirement requires the exact current consumer inventory, nonblank Variable resolution in the executing scope, terminal evidence that consumers used Variables without fallback, explicit deletion selection and post-change readback. Preserve least-privilege review for any credential capable of writing repository secrets; the historical GH_PAT finding is not proof of present permissions. Retired provider keys and exclusion-manifest changes require their own scoped disposition. No historical DELETED or still-present table establishes current configuration, and no values belong in this documentation.

interpretations.heading: Inherited public-entry and commercial controls
interpretations.text: Keep public signup, repeat sign-in and recovery, useful first Private session, immutable trial grant/expiry and client-clock negatives, paid continuation, checkout-to-entitlement persistence across refresh/sign-out, portal access, cancellation, unpaid/past_due/failure handling, duplicate/replayed webhooks and RPC failure handling as distinct acceptance controls. A test-mode journey can establish functional behavior; it does not activate production payments. Activation still requires both payment switches, aligned live configuration and webhook/price/entitlement verification under explicit owner authority. Real-money transactions are not required proof or a launch gate. Historical Free/Basic, Cloud/Native, sample, 2h/day and 50h/month policies are superseded by the current one-product commercial contract, not new exceptions.

interpretations.heading: Clause receiving record and evidence limits
interpretations.text: The documentation clause receiving artifact is an attributed record of what predecessor documents said, not an executed test ledger. Each record binds exact source text and hash to the retained meaning, exact canonical interpretation and superseding authority. Original reported PASS/FAIL/HOLD, metrics, rejected candidates and missing /private/tmp receipts remain distinguishable. Documentary quotation preserves provenance; it does not independently verify an execution or establish a baseline regression. R5/r14 and the distinction between campaign R4 and true campaign 3-R4C require the correctly bound originals and independent review; overlay labels cannot establish a regression. The original source documents remain undeleted until the separate removal decision.

interpretations.heading: Historical browser trace interpretation
interpretations.text: The 23 May trace brief used synthetic macOS speech through local preview/CDP. Native duplication improved but provider-final content remained wrong; successful save and a polished score did not establish transcript quality. Private first visible text was reported at 10.527 seconds, with missed opening fillers and noise/tail hallucinations despite earlier chunks reaching inference. Cloud remained disabled under a PRO badge, so that run measured an admission/UI mismatch, not provider quality. Preserve those separate findings, the input and artifact identities; none is a current customer-engine verdict. Current customer transcription is Private-only, and the surviving onset, tail, timing, save and evidence-validity controls are in STT and QUALITY.

interpretations.heading: Private STT experiment interpretation
interpretations.text: Keep the June STT-P1/P1D/P5/P6/P7/P8 histories separate. P5's equal 87.5% result fell back to RMS and did not test Silero; WASM MIME/HTML failures were setup failures. P6 first failed on HTML assets, then on unsupported model type, before v2-compatible models ran. Base improved h1_6 to 100%, while small was rejected after 87.5% with 46,728ms finalization; the later enriched base proof still lost the leading filler and reported 123,159ms Washington finalization versus 12,614ms tiny with equal 99.48% accuracy. These are different runs, not one winning baseline. Human requests for base that actually recorded tiny remain tiny evidence. P8's box/linear comparisons showed timing changes but no accuracy lift, and easy perfect guard rows did not test the original casualty. Decode-parameter A/B worsened 25% WER to 100% and was rejected.

interpretations.heading: Private lifecycle and filler evidence interpretation
interpretations.text: P1D's filler-count improvement did not close repeated or order-wrong saved speech: the later partial proof still lost/moved opening Um and retained extra trailing words, despite a loose browser test passing. P7 controller grace did not fix the separate service frozen warning; the subsequent injected smoke passed but omitted the heartbeat trace, and human proof remained distinct. The original Private CI proof reported 51.72% WER after successful save, while v4 produced an empty candidate; neither was an authentication-only failure. Preserve the earlier human 56.36% accuracy / 66.67% filler recall and empty-detail observation separately from later injected save/detail passes. Hard-navigation loss and rapid-churn render-loop FAILs remain original outcomes, not silently closed by model improvements.

interpretations.heading: Model, runtime and contamination interpretation
interpretations.text: The earlier 93.89% clean-file tiny result bypassed the browser mic path and is not a universal model ceiling. Mic-DSP repeats gave raw 75% / 25% and browser-default 75% / 75%, so they did not justify a default change. Thread/WebGPU acceleration hypotheses did not measure a speedup. Preserve v4 q4/WASM data-location failures, successful Node isolates and later browser dtype/single-thread evidence as different runtime experiments; none alone proves product promotion. Preserve Moonshine run1/run2 FAILs, the missing run2 exit, and the later 5% tolerance interpretation without rewriting the original byte-instability result. One 12-second loader/zero-body-byte proof is neither model quality nor complete privacy. Frozen 600 timing contamination leaves performance unmeasured until score-identical quiet reruns; smoke 85, preflight 459 and frozen 10,894 reference words are distinct denominators.

interpretations.heading: Historical release and audit interpretation
interpretations.text: PL-001–011 and the June closeout contain dated entry, billing, trial, feedback/PDF, viewport and observability observations, not current launch clearance. Physical mobile/touch remained unproved; viewport images, PDF affordances and transport acknowledgements cannot replace device, parsed-export or persistence evidence. The old 35-account inventory and Dev-none-in-flight statement are not current state. Preserve original A1–A6 backlog decisions and requested evidence through the current receiver, without selecting old v4 targeting, broad branch deletion or account cleanup. The historical 615-file / 6,158-case catalog and 97-document ledger are snapshots, not current denominators. Source-built Progress, privacy boundaries or compliance collateral do not establish a moat, demand, willingness to pay, retention or a commercial advantage.

interpretations.heading: Rejected design and integration receipts
interpretations.text: The withdrawn first #1314 packet, later additive-RPC correction and original two-transcript design remain separate documentary stages. Preserve the ambiguity/partial-apply/rollback casualties; do not apply a superseded migration packet as current procedure. The case1/case7 handoffs preserve original red controls, known-interrupted versus unknown-stage behavior, received failure binding and cap negatives; later test totals are reported receipts, not fresh execution here. The paired-evaluator handoff requires an independently frozen manifest×trial population and rejects shared missing/duplicate/substituted rows; completeness does not approve its statistics, corpus or model. The attribution sanitation crosswalk remains a distinct lookup for old/new identities and signature limitations; it does not settle the separately missing historical tag chronology.

interpretations.heading: Predecessor decisions and remaining receiving ownership
interpretations.text: #1674 receives retained documentation and acceptance obligations from predecessor packets; transferred issue wrappers and completed prose do not complete product requirements. Jensen receives non-documentation controls with original IDs, evidence, next action and dependency; Cloud separately owns its harness. Old release/dev branch assignments, post-merge cleanup proposals and experimental tuning sequences are historical and confer no new work or operational authority. R01–R16 post-RWT ideas remain a distinct proposal register with original identifiers and explicit owner disposition; semantic coaching efficacy, felt progress and willingness to pay are not inferred from metric movement. Promotional draft copy and video assets require release-specific claim checking and separate publication/provider-spend authorization.

interpretations.heading: Genuine paid-fixture acceptance boundary
interpretations.text: For a separately authorized genuine paid canary, bind the exact profile to nonblank customer/subscription identities and independently read Stripe: that subscription belongs to that customer, is active, and contains the approved active monthly Price, configured currency, 1,000-unit amount and interval count 1. Local profile fields alone are not Stripe authority. Preserve the one-account ceiling and no recording/trial reset or extension. Wrong identity, status or Price, an active conflicting run, or an uncertain response is HOLD. The old #1288 paid-only cutover, 05:00 schedule and immediate-merge sequence are historical; current canary scheduling and trial/test-mode lanes are governed by OPERATIONS_AND_SECURITY. This receipt neither authorizes an entitlement mutation nor activates payments.

interpretations.heading: Inherited commercial-remediation acceptance matrix
interpretations.text: The #1290 audit contributes controls beyond billing configuration: trial-active and paid fixtures must ignore exhausted legacy sample fields and former accumulated-minute thresholds; only expiry or terminal paid lapse blocks new recording/save/analysis. Both lifecycle states share the 600-second per-recording safety stop and can start again afterward. Entitlement rejects all customer engines except Private. Root-route acquisition, trial labels, expired retained access, dead/reusable marketing surfaces, accessibility labels, exact $10 pricing, and mocks must agree with the server contract. Preserve replay and disposable PostgreSQL 15/16/17 proof for applicable database changes, zero active references to retired policies, desktop/mobile visual evidence and every required CI gate. A deprecated lane must be explicitly retired from the required graph, never waived as an accepted red. Historical migration sequencing and a two-lane every-push canary are superseded by current release and canary controls; source coverage does not close the integrated real-device Practice Loop.

interpretations.heading: Stale-bundle and account-exit receiving controls
interpretations.text: The P0 Private findings came from a stale pre-cutover browser and cannot qualify a later release. Preserve the pre-Start freshness mismatch/unknown negative, missing selector/terminal-state/recognized-text negatives, and the rule that a freshness prompt must not interrupt an active recording. Finalized filler total and chips use one coherent snapshot; empty measured filler data differs from unavailable data. Successful persistence clears Finalizing/candidate state, exact-session review and PDF agree while the transcript is retained, and each completion has one valid next action. Hosted account-exit proof must cover transcript/metrics/history removal, telemetry unlinking, immediate token denial, service-only tombstone/retry behavior and legacy-RPC bypass removal; PGlite alone cannot close hosted Auth. The predecessor three-session protocol used at least 35 seconds and 90 words per same-cohort session; retain this as an inherited qualification fixture, not a replacement for current Progress eligibility. Its newest-two eviction assertion is superseded by newest-one retention; the current receiving run must explicitly prove that policy while preserving the baseline/comparison and residual-metrics controls. Controlled WER artifacts are a distinct authorized evidence boundary, not permission to log speech in diagnostics.

interpretations.heading: Constants and realistic audio-cadence controls
interpretations.text: The historical constants audit separates source sample rate, target STT sample rate, worklet callback cadence, transcription window, retry retention and stop-tail forcing; these are different units and boundaries. Derive sample counts from the selected rate and duration, record actual source/target rates and frame cadence, and test quiet speech, room noise, silence and retained retry audio with realistic frames. A giant test frame cannot establish worklet timing. Preserve distinct first-text, ongoing heartbeat and finalization controls. The May table mixed a working tree, committed values and older observations; its numeric values and proposed module are not current runtime authority. Current checked-in constants and selected Private path govern. Historical Cloud packet/reconnect values and Native restart settings remain research evidence, not restored customer modes.

interpretations.heading: Native and Cloud historical qualification limits
interpretations.text: The May 25 synthetic browser run reported Private first text 9.783s, Native 8.655s with only a weak partial, and Cloud 9.670s after correcting account entitlement. Clean console/network counts did not establish useful text or meet the then-defined Private <6s target. The May 25 Native reviewer packet described non-continuous recognition as RC-red; the May 26 second opinion reported a later human continuous-recognition journey, explicitly withheld Edge equivalence and rejected fake-device WER without proof that the fixture reached Web Speech. These are different observations, not one corrected PASS. The June Native report still had empty detail despite a 55-word saved transcript and 853ms formatter; reported 35/35 frontend and 73/73 Edge steps, then 68/68 and 31/31 subsets, did not close human detail/truecasing. The June Cloud report recorded ~91.86% corrected target versus ~91.53% app corpus, 44/44 local contracts and one 46.2s deployed smoke; full tail/readability/WER proof remained open. Pre-fix trust-label contamination must not be attributed to a later head without reproof. These legacy provider paths, localhost-only gates, pricing and launch priorities do not override the current Private-only product or canonical deployment binding.

interpretations.heading: Historical identity diagnosis and manual-unblock limit
interpretations.text: Gate B records five distinct fixes: identity invocation, initialization order, ingested-event materialization, an ineffective flush attempt and immediate capture. Its initial bot-filter explanation was an inference without the exact harness UA/driver readback; the later human-login resolution and targeted/negative stacked proof are separate evidence. A queryable received identity event is stronger than a local identify call or a flags request. The reported targeted v4 WER 0.1099 and RTF 0.0760 versus default-v2 WER 0.0890, with save/detail/post-stop integrity, describe that stacked test build. They do not establish a durable automated identity harness, a production model promotion or current PostHog selection authority. Preserve the API lesson: confirm an SDK method in its declared public contract; a guarded nonexistent flush call is not transport proof. Old targeting/UA-masking/admin-repair procedures confer no current authority.

interpretations.heading: v4 runtime chronology and surviving experiment controls
interpretations.text: The June recovery matrices reported q8 session creation failing on a missing decoder scale and q4 failing with invalid data location. Node isolates decoded successfully, but single-thread/no-proxy browser repeats still failed, falsifying that proposed browser fix; later exact-contract failures had blank runtime version fields. Preserve those FAILs alongside the later reported WASM decode in run 27305398130 and the separate detail/403 issue and claimed #85 resolution. They cannot be collapsed into a universal WASM failure, an authentication-only failure or a fully qualified browser success. A runtime experiment must first produce nonempty text and observed version/dtype/device/model-file identity, then test app save/detail equality and the intended hardware. Strict override failures, one-shot AUTO fallback success and actual candidate success are separate outcomes. The old three-gate flag readiness, 93.89% threshold, PostHog selector, branch commands and GPU dispatches are superseded operational instructions, not selected work. Preserve the controlled model/device/dtype/main-thread-versus-worker hypothesis matrix as experiment design only; do not enact its proposed fixes without a matching casualty and approved experiment.

interpretations.heading: Complete product-quality measurement boundary
interpretations.text: A model score or privacy property alone does not establish useful transcription. Preserve setup/auth/input/runtime identity; first progress, first useful text and stop-to-detail timing; word completeness, semantic substitutions and app-versus-direct differences; filler recall and false insertion; punctuation, capitalization, run-on length and duplication; visible/final/saved/detail equality; and truthful provisional/final copy as separate controls. Historical Cloud/Native baselines can inform a controlled comparison only when their route and identity are valid; they are not current customer offerings or mandatory newly authorized provider runs. Original numeric targets remain dated evidence unless the current predeclared policy explicitly adopts them.

interpretations.heading: Selection-harness evidence boundary
interpretations.text: The June idle-selection audit distinguished a seven-minute unbounded harness wait from the product selection path. Its useful controls survive: selecting a policy while idle must not unexpectedly initialize/download a model; state and policy updates must not let a previous selection overwrite the requested one; cancellation and lifecycle-version checks must prevent late work. The old Pro/Free/sample dropdown and Cloud-preservation implementation are historical, not current customer UI requirements. Current selection attribution must use the checked-in authority and observed pre-Start locking/fallback rules, not a passing obsolete switching test.

interpretations.heading: Moonshine loader and window receipts
interpretations.text: The engine-runtime proof found and corrected a ModelArch token/member mismatch that fake-transcriber tests could not detect. Both arches reportedly produced different component requests and genuine live-window versus final output on one 12.23-second clip; seven pinned assets per arch and zero request bodies bound that observation. runtimeVersion and assetIdentity were null in the loaded transcriber, so attribution came from intercepted asset URLs/digests, not the session record. The separate windowed E/F runs used seven verified warm-cache components with no network fallback, a clean 38-word reference rather than the filler fixture, and retained original FAIL verdicts. E2 differed across runs and E3 failed both; the final word varied while earlier words agreed. The later 1/38 (2.63%) drift interpretation under a 5% rule does not rewrite the exact-equality failure or prove corpus/device quality. Preserve the corrected pin-source citation, the uncaptured second exit code and the original payloads/digests; exact reproducibility and broader promotion are separate.

July 10 Option D later reported functional QA-GO on 899161b2, distinct from the owner’s overall invite/release decision. interpretations.text: The dated code/strategy audit found an implemented acceptance-to-next-session association and same-cohort movement calculation, not causal coaching efficacy. Preserve the distinction between browser-local STT and separately disclosed server-side text/coaching processing. Progress/source coverage, waitlist infrastructure, compliance tests and local-inference cost hypotheses do not establish demand, willingness to pay, lower churn or defensibility. interpretations.heading: Lifecycle trace completeness and historical baseline limits
interpretations.text: Bind engine emission, service receipt, controller state, store update, visible text, stop selection, save and detail to the same session and observation window. Preserve the stop-selected source and visible/selected/payload/saved lengths, with first broken boundary or explicit not-captured status. A populated trace schema is harness validation, not transcript quality. The finalized filler snapshot belongs to the terminal persistence/reconciliation join, never a stale intermediate buffer. The old baseline recorded 10/10 persistence with 0/10 history/detail as a harness gap, not a proven save failure; focused loop-free Native rows still had 37.5–80% accuracy, while the Private 92.75% browser drop-in versus 88.47% first-four app comparison still needed a full clean corpus. Historical provider prompts, sample policy and a 90-second finalization allowance cannot set current defaults or close present acceptance. Current saved-transcript integrity forbids ambiguous destructive collapse; downstream History/PDF must reflect the authoritative retained result. Numeric targets and score eligibility require their actual current definition, not an old universal score or an uncited vendor comparison.

interpretations.heading: 5a. Metric definition matrix (#1265)
interpretations.text:
## 5a. Metric definition matrix (#1265)

Every displayed and persisted delivery metric has **one** definition, shared across session review, telemetry, stored data, Progress, and the PDF. The comparability floor and the quality-mapping tunables live in code as the single source of truth (`frontend/src/utils/aggregateProgress.ts`), and nothing else in the client defines the floor. `tests/config/progress-metric-consistency.test.ts` fails if this table drifts from those constants or a second definition appears.

| Metric | Unit | Quality mapping (0..1) | Direction | Code constant |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filler rate | fillers/min | linear to 0 at **10** fillers/min; lower is better | lower = better | `FILLER_RATE_ZERO_QUALITY = 10` |
| Clarity | 0..100 | the value itself (÷100); higher is better | higher = better | `sessions.clarity_score` (evidence input, never a user score) |
| Pace | words/min (WPM) | inside the band **[130, 150]** = 1; linear falloff over **60** WPM outside | banded (faster is not blindly better) | `PACE_IDEAL = [130,150]` (the shared 130–150 authority — `ANALYTICS_THRESHOLDS.TARGET_WPM_MIN/MAX`), `PACE_TOLERANCE = 60` |
| Pause rhythm | % of session that is silence | inside the band **[5, 20]%** = 1; linear falloff over **20** pp outside | banded | `SILENCE_IDEAL = [5,20]`, `SILENCE_TOLERANCE = 20` |

**Comparability rules (both gates):**
- **Duration gate:** a session counts toward comparison/trend only at **≥ 30 s** spoken (`MIN_COMPARABLE_SECONDS = 30`, defined once). This is distinct from the 3-word *computability* rule and the persistence floor (§4).
- **Mode gate:** only compatible sessions are compared. **Open Mic delivery progress and Focus Points coverage are separate measures** and are never mixed into one number.
- **Comparison targets:** the **previous comparable session** for near-term change, with the **first comparable session** preserved as baseline context. A signal is included only when it has valid evidence in **both** sessions.

---

interpretations.heading: 5.1 Default-off integration and served-release binding
interpretations.text:
### 5.1 Default-off integration and served-release binding

The selected release policy separates serial source integration from production promotion.
The workflow mechanics in §5 describe the installed default-off source controls and deliberate
promotion route; they do not certify provider settings or the served-release variable.
Verify actual source and provider trigger posture before landing any PR; source controls
alone do not establish safe provider bootstrap or grant production permission.
Until the bootstrap is safe, keep landings **HOLD** and
continue independent source/tests/documentation work.

**Integration order.** Finish the increment and its new feature/regression tests; obtain
applicable runtime/test evidence and ordinary `ci.yml` full-evidence PASS on the exact
candidate head; then obtain independent review of that head. Separately verify that the
production mutation route remains OFF: `deploy_production=false` skips the production
policy/validation/deployment jobs and supplies no test or full-evidence PASS. The ordinary
CI workflow has no `deploy_production` input. Review-dependent qualification follows the
review and must also be green before merge. Land one protected, latest-main PR at a time,
verify main green, then advance the queue. A changed, rebased or conflict-resolved head
requires renewed tests and review. Documentation-only work needs applicable documentation
checks and independent review; workflow/configuration behavior is not a documentation-only
exception. A no-deploy merge is source integration, not a production release or live proof.

**Bootstrap prerequisite.** Before the first gate landing, the responsible operator must
establish an explicitly authorized way to prevent unintended production deployment under
the *existing* Actions and Vercel Git/build triggers. Adding a false-default workflow input
does not itself control Vercel's separate Git integration. Identify the exact settings or
bootstrap operation, its operator, authority and readback; missing evidence keeps landing
**HOLD**. This procedure grants no settings or production permission.

The scheduled-monitor binding is the non-secret repository Actions Variable
`PRODUCTION_RELEASE_SHA`, catalogued in
[OPERATIONS_AND_SECURITY.md §2.3](./OPERATIONS_AND_SECURITY.md#23-github-actions-env-home-d--secrets-vs-variables).
Bootstrap requires a fresh observation of production's `window.__APP_RELEASE__`, reconciled
with the last successful authorized release and its required qualification/readback evidence.
Use the full 40-character SHA; do not infer it from repository `main`, a merge receipt or a
successful build alone. Verify the selected workflow consumes this variable and obtain
separate authority for its initial write. If identity or release evidence cannot be reconciled,
leave bootstrap unverified and **HOLD** rather than inventing a value.

**Promotion and advancement.** App is the selected production release operator. For an
explicitly authorized promotion, select one exact qualified, independently reviewed,
main-green SHA and the bounded operation. `deploy_production=true` expresses that selection;
it does not replace separate frontend/Edge/migration/secrets/provider/account permissions,
existing confirmations, drain invalidation or mandatory operation readbacks.

1. Record the intended candidate SHA, operation, authorizations and prior verified binding.
   Check current main/qualification and reject drift before any production action.
2. Execute only the separately authorized promotion scope through the installed gated route.
   Preserve the workflow/run attempt, source identity and terminal results.
3. For a frontend promotion, independently observe the served frontend identity; require exact
   equality to the intended SHA and successful readbacks for every selected operation. A frontend
   SHA alone does not prove Edge generation/configuration, database state or account outcomes.
   A backend-only operation requires its own exact-source/runtime readbacks and does not advance
   the frontend binding to an unserved commit.
4. Only after all required promotion/readback checks succeed, have the operator with separately
   authorized repository-variable access advance `PRODUCTION_RELEASE_SHA` to that verified
   served SHA and read the variable back. Retain its previous value until this point.
5. Record the UTC observations, intended/observed SHA, variable readback and linked run/receipts
   in `RELEASE_STATUS.md`. Scheduled monitoring binds to the verified served release; unserved
   later main commits retain their own CI evidence and cannot replace this binding.

**Failure and recovery.** Failed, cancelled, partial or uncertain promotion, or a failed/mismatched
served readback, retains the prior variable and yields **HOLD**. This does not prove that a
partially changed production environment still matches the old value. If deployment succeeds
but the variable update/readback fails, keep the discrepancy visible as **HOLD**; do not claim
monitoring is bound to the new release. Preserve failure history and request the precise
authorized recovery step; no automatic retry, rollback or permission bypass is implied.
Missing/malformed binding or served-identity drift must never silently use latest main or
produce green qualification. Preserve daily/weekly health visibility and mark unavailable
product evidence unexecuted. Serving the expected SHA does not close live/human acceptance.

---

interpretations.heading: 9. Model-selection evidence history
interpretations.text:
## 9. Model-selection evidence history

Model selection is a reproducible decision record, not a winning WER copied from a log. The three evidence sets have different jobs and must never be renamed or blended:

| Evidence set | Exact identity | Permitted use |
|---|---|---|
| Harvard smoke | 10 clips / **85 normalized words** | Pipeline smoke and known-answer characterization only. Never selection evidence. |
| Preflight | 23 clips / **459 normalized words** | Unseen-corpus defect discovery and candidate triage. The planning target was 425 words; 459 is what the deterministic selection produced. Never selection evidence. |
| Frozen selection | **600 utterances / 10,894 normalized words** | Selection-grade accuracy, reliability and performance evidence when every gate below passes. This is not a “600-word test.” |

The 85-word set produced a ceiling effect: several distinct models differed by only one or two errors and some scored zero, so it could not support a ranking. The 459-word set then separated the candidates and exposed corpus/runtime defects before the expensive frozen run. Only the frozen 600-utterance set may drive the down-select, using the decision policy fixed before its results existed.

### Required matrix and artifacts

Every proposed model/configuration has one cell in every evidence set. A cell contains metrics or a named `not_run` / `invalid` / `rejected` reason; absence is never a pass. The matrix retains scored candidates, load failures, unsupported options, aliases, diagnostic duplicates, contaminated runs and hardware-unrepresentative runs. Aliases and diagnostics remain visible but cannot enter a ranking.

For each cell, retain:

- model id, revision, exact asset digests, dtype/quantization, runtime and version;
- lane, requested device, resolved/proven backend, and whether the hardware is representative;
- corpus id, utterance count, normalized reference-word count, normalizer version and Track A/B identity;
- pooled WER, substitutions, deletions, insertions, reference words, and all reliability counters;
- cold load, warm-decode p50/p95, RTF p50/p95, actual downloaded bytes, and peak memory or an explicit `unmeasured`;
- short- and long-form integrity, including truncation, preserved tail and repetition checks;
- contamination state, selection eligibility and the named reason for any exclusion; and
- per-utterance score/timing data sufficient to reproduce pooled totals and paired bootstrap intervals without decoding again.

The evidence has four durable layers:

1. immutable raw artifacts with per-utterance data and exact execution identity;
2. a versioned registry at `tests/STT_BENCHMARKS.json` containing every matrix cell;
3. a dated human-readable report indexed by `EVIDENCE_INDEX.md`; and
4. the current primary/fallback product contract in this document after Product Owner approval.

The dated report must distinguish the product baseline, measurement execution tree and selection-policy tree. It must explain the 85-word ceiling, the defects and requalifications found at 459 words, the complete 600-utterance results, and how paired bootstrap intervals produced a winner or a statistical tie. It reports three separate conclusions: **technical winner**, **MVP activation readiness**, and **failure-diverse fallback**. Integration convenience cannot change the technical ranking.

SwiftShader proves WebGPU compatibility only; it is not hardware performance evidence. Rows from different corpora, normalizers, runtime versions or evidence classes cannot be ranked together. A contaminated timing is `unmeasured`, not slow or fast. The quiet reruns for contaminated `v2:tiny.en` and `v2:base.en` may replace performance fields only after every per-utterance score profile reconciles; any accuracy difference invalidates the replacement.

Historical results are append-only. When a harness, model asset or inference runtime is later found defective, preserve the old row, mark it invalid with the reason and link the requalification. Never delete the evidence that explains why an earlier decision changed.

---

clauses.source_section: Retained benchmark evidence / Retention is mandatory
clauses.source_clause:
A measuring run retains by default. Omitting `--out` no longer discards the result — the runner derives

`canary-identity-config` guard fails closed unless both canary email Variables are valid/distinct/
non-prohibited **and** both canary password Secrets are present (value never logged); the flawless-launch
guard statically fails on any active `secrets.*_EMAIL` for these four names or the retired canary password.
Operator state (verified): the four email **Secrets are deleted**, the four email **Variables are
configured**, and all four password Secrets are present. Admin, canary, RC gates, benchmarks, and
live-release workflows must not be dispatched on a `main` that still reads the deleted email Secrets —
dispatch only after this cutover merges.

That is the most dangerous single capability in the inventory: a compromise of that job (or a dependency)
could overwrite any repository Secret.

clauses.source_clause:
E2 and E3 in these raw artifacts fail solely because the old probe asserts exact whole-string equality
(`sessionA.final === sessionB.final`), so a single unstable token fails them. That assertion measured
byte determinism, not the accumulating cross-session state E2 claims to detect. #1432 corrects the
acceptance rule without editing these artifacts: reuse must not drift more than the independent A↔C
fresh-instance baseline, and every pair must remain within a 5% word-edit ceiling. The two retained runs
both pass that rule at 1/38 maximum drift (2.63%); a repeated or compounded window fails its casualty.

matching a second session rules out cross-session accumulation.

clauses.source_clause:
- **Blocker:** requires `crossOriginIsolated === true` (COOP/COEP headers). Thread code

  (headers off).** The "Stripe.js blocks it" premise is **CONFIRMED STALE** (checkout is redirect-
  only, not embedded). **Layer-1 static audit (2026-06-30):** `index.html` has ZERO cross-origin
  embeds, fonts are system/self-hosted → the real `credentialless` targets are runtime loads:
  **#1 ORT WASM from jsDelivr** (worker never sets `wasmPaths`; self-host to remove) + PostHog/
  Supabase/Sentry fetch (Bearer/API-key → likely OK). **Multiplier ~2–2.5× UNMEASURED → ~32–36s/5min,
  still over 30s alone.** Remaining: live preview measurement (`crossOriginIsolated===true` + resources + decode speedup).
